  6:41 p.m.

PRESENT  Mayor  Maria  Davila,  Vice  Mayor  Joshua Barron,  Council  Member  Maria
  del Pilar Avalos,  Council  Member  Gil Hurtado  and Council  Member  Al

ABSENT  City Attorney  Raul F. Salinas

WATER  The City  Council  unanimously  received  and filed  the City  of South  Gate
  2025 Public  Health  Goals  ("PHG")  Report,  as required  by the California
  Health  and Safety  Code by motion  of Council  Member  Hurtado  and
  seconded  by Council  Member  Avalos.

  Arturo  Cervantes,  Director  Public  Works,  stated that state law requires
  water  systems  with  over 10,000  connections  to prepare  Public  Health
  Goals  report  every  three years. Mr. Cervantes  stated Chris  Castillo,  Water
  Manager,  will  be making  a presentation.

  Chris  Castillo,  Water Manager,  gave a presentation.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  appreciated  the presentation  including  the
  information  about dark water.  He would  like the residents  to be aware  of
  solicitors  that are trying  to sell water  filters  which  are not necessary.

  Council  Member  Rios asked Mr. Castillo  to elaborate  on the flyer  the
  community  received  a regarding  the water.  He also noticed  a tractor  at the
  Boy  Scouts  and asked if that's  going  to be a treatment  facility.

  Mr. Castillo  explained  the flyer  was to inform  residents  about PFAS  was
  detected  in two of the wells.  The city has six wells.  The PFAS  is above
  health  goal, but below  the standard.  The city can serve that water  per state
  requirements,  the city is actively  pursuing  a design  to treat it.
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF AUGUST  26, 2025

WATER  CONT'D  Mr. Cervantes  stated the city is required  by state law to issue that flyer.

  Council  Member  Avalos  sits on the Southeast  Water  Coalition  stated that

  3M has paid 1.1 million  dollars  toward  the treatment  of the PFAS  and the

  congresswoman  allocated  some funding  for the PFAS  treatment  plant the

  city is planning  to build.

  Mayor  Davila  asked if the notice  will  be included  with  the water bill.

  Mr. Castillo  stated that it will  be included  in the water  bill.

  Mayor  Davila  asked if anyone  in the audience  wished  to speak on this
  item.

  Liz Ruiz thanked  everyone  for the presentation  and is glad for the
  treatment.

  Having  no one else come forward,  Mayor  Davila  closed  the audience
  portion.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  thanked  Mr. Castillo  for the presentation.  It is very

  important  to continue  educating  the residents  on this issue.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  recommended  a movie  called  Dark  Waters

  showing  how PFAS  got into the water  system.
